Silver miners are sitting on a record cash pile:

Net cash balance across the top 10 silver mining companies surged to a record ~$4.2 billion in Q2 2026.

This figure has more than doubled since Q3 2025.

This marks a sharp reversal from the 2014-2024 period, when debt exceeded cash levels for most quarters.

To put this into perspective, during the 2010-2011 rally, combined net cash balance among these companies never exceeded $2.0 billion.

Cash accumulation has accelerated sharply alongside the silver rally, as higher silver prices have boosted margins and free cash flow across the group.

Silver miners have never been this liquid.

It is bad practice to fade breakouts to new all-time highs.

New all-time highs are uncharted territory. 

They are the path of least resistance. Meaning there are no cost areas above these levels. Price can extend, extend... until a cost area forms. 

So when you see a breakout to new all-time high... start with this:

What could the market know that I'm not aware of?

Not saying it will be a similar move, but imagine the number of people that tried to fade that Gold breakout. Certain that it was a bull trap. 

When your most recent evidence is suggesting a breakout to new highs, you are better off taking that into account until new evidence emerges...
